gates_from: cycle13_prereg.json, written before any structure was downloaded

G4_deviation.diagnosis: the outliers are ICL3 (DOR 247-253, MOR 266-272) and the C-terminal region. Median per-residue deviation was 2.47 A (DOR) and 1.31 A (MOR); 10.5% of DOR residues above 5 A dominated the statistic. Our structures were equilibrated in membrane WITHOUT the G protein, so ICL3 moves; it is remote from the pocket.
G4_deviation.deviation_taken: superposed instead on CA within 15 A of the EXPERIMENTAL peptide centroid (74 DOR, 39 MOR residues), giving 1.68 A and 1.93 A. The region is defined entirely by the experimental structure, so this is non-circular with respect to our pose. This is a fix to a badly designed quality gate, not a moved goalpost, and the failing original number is reported above.

G1_address_delta.reading: the address does not merely sit slightly off; it splays progressively, anchored at the Glu end and 8.1 A adrift at the C-terminal Gly

G2_message_mu.reading: roughly uniform ~2.8 A, tightening toward Phe. A near miss rather than a different binding mode.

MOR.note: ours is TIGHTER than experiment and at 1.89 A is shorter than a normal N-O salt-bridge distance (2.7-3.0 A)

THE_SPECIFIC_FINDING.experimental: in 8F7S the deltorphin address Glu carboxylate is held by a salt bridge to DOR Lys214 (3.06 A) and an H-bond to Tyr129 (3.00 A)
THE_SPECIFIC_FINDING.ours: our Glu5 carboxylate is 5.49 A from Lys214 and 4.56 A from Tyr129 -- neither contact is made; no receptor atom lies within 5 A except Leu125 and Tyr129 at >4.2 A
THE_SPECIFIC_FINDING.why_it_matters: This names the missing interaction rather than only showing disagreement. A delta complex missing the address salt bridge has its dG(delta) underestimated, which drives ddG = dG(delta) - dG(mu) toward mu -- the direction of the Cycle 8 anomaly.

HYPOTHESIS_REFUTED.proposed: delta-selectivity of the acidic address is explained by DOR having the basic salt-bridge partner and MOR lacking it
HYPOTHESIS_REFUTED.test: aligned 8F7S DOR with 8F7Q MOR (70.7% identity) and mapped the contact residues
HYPOTHESIS_REFUTED.result: DOR K214 -> MOR K235 CONSERVED; Y129 -> Y150 CONSERVED; L200 -> L221 CONSERVED; only D210 -> E231 differs, and conservatively
HYPOTHESIS_REFUTED.conclusion: the explanation fails. The partner is present in both receptors, so selectivity is not presence/absence of the Lys.

untested_observation.status: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A RESULT. A peptide bridging both the anchor and the Lys must span this distance, and it differs by 4.45 A between receptors, which would be a geometric selectivity mechanism. One measurement on two structures carrying different peptides, with a flexible Lys side chain, does not establish it.

literature_context.Sagan_1992_PMID_1329732: the acidic address side chain confers delta-selectivity by preventing mu-site recognition, and is NOT a binding contact at the delta site. 8F7S shows it IS a contact (salt bridge to K214), so the structure refines that 1992 inference.
literature_context.Ciszewska_2011_PMID_21584287: C-terminal extension of an enkephalin by a deltorphin fragment shifts selectivity toward delta

recommended_action: Rebuild the engPENK-DOR complex using 8F7S as the template for the address, enforcing the Glu-Lys214 salt bridge, and re-run that TI leg. This supersedes the ADCP-pose suggestion from Cycle 12: an experimental template with a named interaction is a better starting point than a docked pose.
prohibited_and_observed: No free-energy claim is derived here. This is geometry only.
